## HERA — Step 4: electron-side D ≈ 0 Landau fan (`landau-fan-vti`)

> **05:23** · landau-fan-vti: D=0, electron n +2.6..+3.2e12 (22), B +0.9..+8 T (100 uniform-1/B), sr1 50 uV, fast\_delay 2.1 s · **ETA ~08:38** (≈3h15m)

Runs 6–7 are complete (ana cells 14–15). Run 6 at n = +3.2×10¹² cm⁻² has a ≈7 T feature plus ≈15, 22, 30 T peaks, several near its harmonics; the one-density peak set does not identify a pocket count. The hole side is capped at |n| ≤1.27×10¹² by the TG validator and is in the investigation's low-density exception regime. I am taking the electron side, n = +2.6…+3.2×10¹² at calibrated D = 0 (run 5), to distinguish true branch trajectories from harmonics and compare the resulting F(n) to the ABAB/ABCA model and F_L.

**Design floor:** the model ABAB partner is 5.41 T at n = 2.6 and 7.31 T at 3.2; F_L,max = 33.1 T. B = 0.9→8 T gives Δ(1/B) = 0.986 T⁻¹, or 5.33 periods for the smallest model partner. 100 uniform-1/B rows give 0.00996 T⁻¹ spacing, 3.03 samples per F_L period at n_max. Twenty-two n points (Δn = 0.0286×10¹²) give 3.0 samples per fourfold LL spacing at 0.9 T. The 1/B resolution over the full window is ≈1.01 T; if the high-frequency tone only survives above 1.5 T, its usable resolution is ≈1.85 T. The fan is floored at n≥2.6; lower electron density would leave fewer than five periods for the ABAB partner and cannot support the same count claim. The upper 2 T of the spot check is excluded because it buys little extra 1/B span, costs ~15 min of ramp, and raises the low-n, high-B dynamic-range risk. Fixed sr1 50 µV (5 kΩ at 10 nA) inherits run 6; its 8 T Rxx was ≈400–500 Ω at n=3.2, so inspect the n=2.6 corner for clipping. `fast_delay=2.1 s` is 7τ at the recorded τ=0.3 s, 24 dB/oct; run 5's 63×66 gatemap took 81.2 min at 1 s fast delay, and runs 6–7 measured the field traverse. Estimated wall time ≈3 h 15 m, including the initial 0→0.9 T positioning ramp (~7 min), 0.9→8 T measured traverse (~52 min), 2200 gate points, row turnaround, and margin.

The cell prints temperature, vaporizer, field, gates, Si, magnet state, lock-in settings, and NPLC before moving; it stops on mismatch. It leaves B at 8 T for a possible measured return leg and parks TG/BG at zero. **Checkpoints:** inspect the first 2–3 rows for drain-current continuity, TG/BG leakage, railing and field tracking; then inspect rows near B≈2, 4, 6 T for emerging oscillations, clipping, and temperature drift. Abort on sustained leakage >1 nA or an instrument anomaly; any magnet interrupt requires an actual field readback before further moves. The FFT and stacking read follow the completed TSV in the ana notebook.

magnet.field(float(B_vec[0]))
